newsitem.title: POLAND: OECD sees Poland exceeding 96-97 inflation goals.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees Poland exceeding 96-97 inflation goals.

text.p: Poland is likely to overshoot its 1996 and 1997 inflation targets and has a chance of sustaining growth at five percent annually in the next two years following a probable 5.5 percent expansion this year, the OECD said.

"A slight overshooting of the official 1996 inflation target (of 17 percent) is likely. For 1997, the government has announced an end-year target of 13 percent, on the way to single-digit inflation in 1998," the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development said in a report.

"In principle, those objectives are within reach, but the OECD Secretariat projects that on current policies they may again be slightly exceeded," it said in its year-end economic outlook for its 28 member countries, published on Thursday.
Growth was later likely to stabilise at around five percent if government policies supported the supply side and if external demand, especially in the European Union, proved strong enough.

It said the recorded trade deficit widened this year following a shift from net exports to domestic consumption and investment because of weak export markets, lower tariffs, growth in real incomes and a stronger zloty.
But it said the rates of growth of imports and exports should gradually converge in 1997 becuase of the expected stabilisation of the real zloty exchange rate.
